2025 Sustainability Report Overview An Innovation Pioneer Sustainable Business Practices A Responsible Purchaser Operations and Governance A Practitioner of Green Power An Admired Employer Appendix Power to Change Society Letter from the ESG Steering Committee Chairperson The rapid acceleration of artiﬁcial intelligence and high-performance computing has ushered the global technology sector into an era of unprecedented computational demand. Electricity powers tokens, and tokens generate intelligence, bringing boundless opportunities as well as pressing challenges for low-carbon transition. To deliver on our environmental commitments, the role of responsible corporate citizenship is more vital than ever. As the world’s leading semiconductor foundry, we embrace our responsibility to provide customers with cutting-edge technology and needed capacity. The next-generation, sustainable products we manufacture continue to lead the industry in

foundry, we embrace our responsibility to provide customers with cutting-edge technology and needed capacity. The next-generation, sustainable products we manufacture continue to lead the industry in density and energy eﬃciency, empowering our customers to unleash their innovation. According to Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), the energy-saving beneﬁts enabled by TSMC-powered ICT products across six smart applications will save more than 180 billion kWh of electricity globally and reduce nearly 89 million metric tons of carbon emissions in 2025. By 2030, for every kilowatt-hour (kWh) of electricity TSMC consumes to manufacture semiconductors, we will save nearly seven kWh. Over the past year, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) issued a landmark advisory opinion, ﬁrmly establishing nations' legal obligations to address climate change. This marks the ﬁrst time in history that climate responsibility has oﬃcially risen

ce (ICJ) issued a landmark advisory opinion, ﬁrmly establishing nations' legal obligations to address climate change. This marks the ﬁrst time in history that climate responsibility has oﬃcially risen to the level of a legal obligation, underscoring that the climate crisis is an urgent and existential threat to humanity. While our manufacturing footprint requires careful management, the environmental value of our technology extends far beyond our cleanrooms. TSMC takes its responsibilities seriously. As part of our commitment to global environmental sustainability, we aligned our netzero roadmap with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) absolute emission targets this year. In parallel, we are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and innovative workplace to meet these challenges. We are also allocating more of our earnings toward sustainability, investing in long-term ESG initiatives, and collaborating with our stakeholders to driv

nnovative workplace to meet these challenges. We are also allocating more of our earnings toward sustainability, investing in long-term ESG initiatives, and collaborating with our stakeholders to drive collective social progress. Sustainability cannot be a passive goal. It requires the same structural discipline, rigorous accountability, and execution focus that we apply to our technology development. For TSMC, sustainability is the cornerstone of our operational resilience, competitiveness, and long-term value. Every step we take toward this sustainable vision relies on the TSMC team aligning toward a common goal. Driven by technology, expertise, and passion, we are working together to make a meaningful, positive impact on the world. C.C. Wei Chairman and Chief Executive Oﬃcer/ ESG Steering Committee Chairperson 4

2025 Sustainability Report Overview An Innovation Pioneer Sustainable Business Practices A Responsible Purchaser Operations and Governance A Practitioner of Green Power An Admired Employer Appendix Power to Change Society Letter from the ESG Committee Chairperson According to the latest Global Risks Report 2026 from the World Economic Forum, the world is entering an "Age of Competition," marked by declining stability in cooperation mechanisms. Rising competition is adding to global turbulence, leading to future risks including extreme climate events, biodiversity loss, and ecosystem collapse. TSMC aligns with the Forward Faster Initiative of the UN Global Compact (UNGC) and its focus on climate action and water resilience. The Company acts on its three sustainability commitments of Net Zero, Water Positive, and No Net Loss (NNL) of Nature and Biodiversity, and collaborates with stakeholders to address these shared global challenges. In response to the global consensus on transition to environmental sustainability, TSMC joined the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) in 2025. The Company adopted innovative emissions reduction solutions throughout each step of its manufacturing process, expanded Scope 3 emissions management , and allocated NT$ 160 million to a carbon reduction subsidy program supporting the supply chain's net-zero roadmap. To conserve water resources, TSMC also continued to improve water eﬃciency and pioneered Taiwan's ﬁrst cross-regional reclaimed water exchange model among industrial users. Guided by a vision of industry growth in harmony with nature, TSMC demonstrated its commitment through the Nature and Biodiversity NNL Action Blueprint . The Company also continued projects such as the Plant-A-Tree Program and the Eco Plus! Ecological Harmony Program , investing in ecological talent development and environmental education while helping communities act as hubs that connect conservation networks. Putting people ﬁrst and building an inclusive environment that respects human rights, safety, and health is our mission. In 2025, based on the results of the Workplace Human Rights Climate Survey, TSMC launched improvement actions at the company and organizational levels , embedding human rights management into daily operations. sed on the results of the Workplace Human Rights Climate Survey, TSMC launched improvement actions at the company and organizational levels , embedding human rights management into daily operations. The Company also held its ﬁrst Global Inclusive Workplace Month to strengthen employee engagement and a sense of belonging. At the same time, TSMC advanced human rights management in the supply chain by establishing the Supplier Human Rights Management Tracking Platform and issuing the statement on Construction Site Safety at TSMC to protect the health and well-being of supplier and contractor partners. For customers, TSMC is committed to safeguarding customer data and product security, aiming to serve as a trusted service provider. For communities, the Company focuses on environmental rights by establishing a research program on Perﬂuoroalkyl Substance (PFAS) alternatives and an initiative to reduce N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) use. To build an ESG culture across the Company, TSMC plans to integrate ESG indicators into employee performance and compensation systems in 2026, establishing accountability and incentive mechanisms. Beyond its own operations, the Company works closely with the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation and the TSMC Charity Foundation to make advances in ﬁve major areas: Educational Innovation, Community Inclusion, Art and Culture Literacy, Ecological Sustainability, and Health Protection. In addition to following the GRI 3: Material Topics 2021 under the GRI Universal Standards 2021 and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) issued under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) by the World Economic Forum (WEF) and the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group, TSMC also incorporates material information analysis result of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2 and continues to refine its Dynamic & Double Materiality (TDDM) methodology. alysis result of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2 and continues to refine its Dynamic & Double Materiality (TDDM) methodology. Through identification of Impacts, Risks, and Opportunities (IRO), TSMC applies both inside-out and outside- in perspectives to address double materiality — covering both impact materiality and financial materiality. This approach systematically prioritizes sustainability issues and defines the materiality matrix. For further details, please refer to the TSMC Materiality Analysis Report . Through the TDDM methodology, TSMC performs material issue assessments and analysis each year based on varying survey objectives to form a comprehensive survey cycle. In the first year, TSMC collects, surveys, and analyzes issues to identify material sustainability issues. In the following year, the Company reviews changes in trends and interdependencies among material issues to ensure action plans effecti

and analyzes issues to identify material sustainability issues. In the following year, the Company reviews changes in trends and interdependencies among material issues to ensure action plans effectively address evolving needs and capture their impacts. In 2025, 1,468 internal and external stakeholders and 366 managers and employees involved in sustainability participated in the materiality survey. TSMC evaluated stakeholder concerns, impact on organizations, and impact on sustainability, and results from IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2 to identify 15 material issues, which were confirmed by the ESG Committee and reported to the Board of Directors. For each material issue, TSMC has established long-term goals for 2030 and actively tracks performance. Additionally, the Company incorporates material issues into its enterprise risk management process to identify risk factors, trends, severity, and likelihood — enabling

d actively tracks performance. To integrate sustainability goals and culture into daily operations and decision-making, TSMC links ESG indicators to performance management and compensation for senior executives, managers, and non-managerial employees, establishing a top-down accountability and incentive structure. At the senior executive level, TSMC provides Employee Restricted Stock Awards to executives, with a maximum of 110% of their eligible shares each year. 100% of the calculation is based on the company's relative performance to Total Shareholder Return (TSR). Overview 2025 Sustainability Report An Innovation Pioneer Sustainable Business Practices A Responsible Purchaser Appendix Operations and Governance A Practitioner of Green Power An Admired Employer Power to Change Society Taiwan LOT (License-on-Transfer) Industry Alliance The patent system was created to protect inventors’ rights, encourage technological innovation, and advance industrial progress. However, the global semiconductor industry has long been challenged by patent litigation by non-practicing entities (NPEs). These entities neither manufacture products nor conduct R&D or provide goods or services. Instead, their business model relies on acquiring patents and demanding substantial licensing fees from companies, often leveraging the threat of litigation. These approach creates operational pressures and legal burdens, ultimately hindering industry innovation. To address NPE risks, TSMC has signed patent crosslicensing or License

e threat of litigation. These approach creates operational pressures and legal burdens, ultimately hindering industry innovation. To address NPE risks, TSMC has signed patent crosslicensing or License-on-Transfer (LOT) agreements with multiple semiconductor companies, covering more than 318,000 patent assets. Under these agreements, if any party transfers a patent to an NPE, the other parties automatically obtain a license to that patent, forming an eﬀective defensive mechanism. The mechanism is triggered only when a patent is transferred to an NPE, preserving patent value while reducing litigation risk and involving no disclosure of technology or trade secrets, supporting collaboration and protecting supply chain interests. Even when the primary unit operates normally, backup units must remain active to enable immediate switchover in the event of an anomaly. To enhance energy eﬃciency, TSMC initiated the development of a smart standby energy-saving mechanism in 2020, conducting independent temperature ramp-up tests and o

chover in the event of an anomaly. To enhance energy eﬃciency, TSMC initiated the development of a smart standby energy-saving mechanism in 2020, conducting independent temperature ramp-up tests and operator response training for each equipment type. By optimizing the linkage between primary and backup units, backup units automatically enter a smart sleep mode when the primary unit is operating normally, signiﬁcantly lowering standby energy consumption. When an abnormal temperature drop signal from the primary unit is detected, the backup unit immediately initiates a rapid heat-up sequence to reach operating temperature, ensuring uninterrupted tail gas treatment. This mechanism not only lowers standby energy consumption of backup units but also minimizes component wear caused by prolonged hightemperature operation, extending overall system lifespan and enhancing operational stability. Overview 2025 Sustainability Report In anticipation of Taiwan’s total phosphorus eﬄuent discharge standards taking eﬀect in 2027, TSMC acted ahead of schedule by oﬃcially incorporating total phosphorus into its Water Pollution Composite Indicator management framework in 2025.
